summary: getOrElseUpdate's new doc is accurate and matches the implementation; removeRefEq/replaceRefEq rewordings remain accurate (confirmed against TrieMap's overrides); but the new @throws tag on updateWith is malformed (no exception class token, just prose starting with 'the'), which breaks the standard @throws syntax and will render/link incorrectly.

items.issue: The new `@throws` tag is written as `@throws the exception thrown by `remappingFunction` if it fails.` -- Scaladoc's `@throws` tag expects the first token to be the exception class name (see e.g. `@throws NoSuchElementException if ...` elsewhere in this codebase, such as collection/Map.scala:326 and Iterable.scala:229). Here the first token is "the", which Scaladoc will try to resolve as a type and fail to link, producing broken/garbled output instead of a proper exception cross-reference. It also never actually names an exception type, and duplicates the sentence already in the description ("the exception is rethrown") without adding a class name, which is the whole point of `@throws`.
items.suggestion: Use the standard `@throws` form, e.g. `@throws Exception if \`remappingFunction\` throws` (or `@throws Throwable ...` since the propagated exception is whatever remappingFunction throws), dropping the leading "the" and the trailing period per the tag-continuation convention.

items.issue: The `@return` tag ("the value associated with the key: the existing value, the newly computed and stored value, or a value inserted concurrently by another thread") restates the description above almost verbatim, which already opens with "Returns" and fully states all three outcomes. Per house rule, `@return` should be dropped when the description already begins with "Returns" and fully states the return value, keeping it only when it adds an edge case not already in the description.
items.suggestion: Drop the `@return` tag, or trim it to add something the description doesn't already say (there isn't such a detail here).

items.issue: Two consecutive blank Scaladoc lines appear between the description paragraph and the `@param` tags (lines 105-106), which is stray formatting left over from editing.
items.suggestion: Remove the extra blank `*` line so there is only one blank line separating the description from the tags.
